resources.string: A fixed carbon monoxide safety answer when you plan to run a fuel-burning device indoors, without the model.

• A generator, charcoal or gas grill, camping stove or lantern, or fuel heater in a home, garage, carport, basement, shed, tent or camper
• A car or other engine left running in a garage
• Heating a home with a gas oven or stove
• How far a generator must be from doors, windows and vents
Can I run my portable generator in the attached garage if I keep the door open?
Is it safe to use a camping stove inside the tent to cook?
Can we bring the propane heater into the camper overnight?

The answer is always the same reviewed text, with its sources (CDC, US CPSC, NHS) and an emergency number line; it starts with No. only when you ask whether you can do it. Small models told people a generator in a garage was fine with the door open. Electric heaters, installed and vented appliances and a propane stove in a kitchen are left to the model. A message about headaches, dizziness or an alarm going off is a health question and goes to the model as one. Questions in English only. Ported from r4to\'s CO hazard check (BOAR R&D).
